sources.title: Balance trimestral de Criminalidad 2025, 4º Trimestre. Municipios mayores de 20.000 habitantes e islas

method: Crime: Interior Ministry Balance de Criminalidad, 2025 full year, types 1–10 (homicide, assault, kidnapping, sexual offences, robbery, burglary, theft, vehicle theft, drug trafficking), per resident. Published only for municipalities over 20,000 residents.
Crime percentile is population-weighted across those municipalities: 30 means 30% of their residents live somewhere with a lower rate. The value is the same for the whole municipality.
Income: INE ADRH 2024, net income per person, per census section. Percentile is population-weighted across all of Spain and inverted, so 0 = highest income, 100 = lowest.

Location: each H3 res-9 cell belongs to the census section containing its centre (sections smaller than a cell use res 10). Where every section is at least 4 times larger than a coarser cell (countryside), that whole cell goes to the section covering most of it.
caveats: Crime is one number per municipality, and only municipalities over 20,000 residents are published; smaller places have no crime value.
Crime per resident inflates tourist and commuter towns, where many offences involve visitors.
Income is a context indicator, not a measure of street quality or safety; switch it off in the popup if you do not want it in the score.
Data is not live: crime covers the last full year published, income lags about two years.
